title: Multi-stage builds
idea: A multi-stage build uses several `FROM` stages in one Dockerfile. By default only the last stage becomes the image, so build tools stay behind.

analogy.text: A workshop and a shop window. You saw, sand and glue in the workshop; only the finished chair goes in the window.
analogy.breaks: The workshop stays in the build cache and speeds up later builds.

points: Each `FROM` starts a fresh stage; name it with `AS build`.
`COPY --from=build` copies chosen files out of an earlier stage.
Layer caching works inside every stage, so keep slow steps early.
Docker's BuildKit builder skips stages the final stage does not use.

steps.caption: The `build` stage installs every dependency, dev tools included, and copies in the source.
`npm run build` writes the compiled app to `dist/`. That folder is all the app needs from this stage.
A second `FROM` starts a clean `runtime` stage. It installs production dependencies only.
`COPY --from=build` brings `dist/` across. It is the only link between the stages.
The last stage is the image. The compiler and dev dependencies never entered it.
Everything else in `build` is left behind. It stays in the build cache, not in the image.

code.title: Two-stage Dockerfile
code.caption: The Book Store API has no build step today. This assumes a `build` script that compiles into `dist/`.

walk.text: Name the first stage `build`. It holds everything needed to compile.
Install all dependencies, dev tools included, then copy the source.
Run the build script. Its output lands in `/app/dist`.
A second `FROM` starts a fresh image. Nothing from `build` carries over.
Copy only `dist` out of the `build` stage.
Document the port and start the compiled app.

pitfalls: Copy only what runs: `COPY --from=build /app .` drags the whole build stage along.
Each stage starts clean: repeat `WORKDIR` and `ENV` in the stage that needs them.
Keep the runtime stage last; the last `FROM` is the image you get.

quiz.q: A Dockerfile has stages build, then runtime. What does docker build produce?
options: One image: the last stage plus files it copied
One image holding both stages in full
The build stage, because it comes first
quiz.why: Only the last stage becomes the image. Earlier stages contribute files solely through `COPY --from`.

takeaway: Compile where the tools live; ship from a clean stage with only the output.

starters: How much smaller does a multi-stage image get?
